facts.statement: Kaikaifilu lived during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous in what is now northern Antarctica.
facts.quote: Kaikaifilu is an extinct genus of large mosasaurs that lived during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous, in what is now northern Antarctica.

facts.statement: The only known species, K. hervei, was described in 2017 from an incomplete specimen found in the López de Bertodano Formation on Seymour Island, Antarctic Peninsula.
facts.quote: The only species known, K. hervei, was described in 2017 from an incomplete specimen discovered in the López de Bertodano Formation, in Seymour Island, Antarctic Peninsula.

facts.statement: The genus name Kaikaifilu honors Coi Coi-Vilu, a reptilian ocean deity from Mapuche cosmology.
facts.quote: The taxon is named in reference to Coi Coi-Vilu, a reptilian ocean deity of the Mapuche cosmology.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence indicates Kaikaifilu lived in Antarctic waters that may have been below freezing.
facts.quote: Fossil records show that Kaikaifilu lived in waters whose temperatures may have dropped below freezing.

facts.statement: With a maximum estimated length of 10 meters, Kaikaifilu is the largest known mosasaur in the Southern Hemisphere and potentially one of the largest tylosaurines.
facts.quote: The maximum body size would be approximately 10 m long, making Kaikaifilu the largest mosasaur identified in the Southern Hemisphere, as well as one of the largest tylosaurines known to date, if its attribution to this group remains valid.

facts.statement: Kaikaifilu is distinguished by well-marked heterodont dentition, a rare trait among mosasaurs and absent in other tylosaurines.
facts.quote: One of the distinguishing characteristics of this taxon is that it has well-marked heterodont dentition, a trait rarely present in mosasaurs and not found in other tylosaurines.

facts.statement: The sole known specimen, cataloged SGO.PV.6509, was discovered in January 2011 by the Chilean Paleontological Expedition on Seymour Island.
facts.quote: The only known specimen of Kaikaifilu hervei, cataloged as SGO.PV.6509, was discovered in January 2011 by the Chilean Paleontological Expedition in the Upper Maastrichtian beds of the López de Bertodano Formation, located on Seymour Island, in the Antarctic Peninsula.

facts.statement: The species name hervei honors Chilean geologist Francisco Hervé for his contributions to the geology of Chile and the Antarctic Peninsula.
facts.quote: The specific epithet hervei is named in honor of Francisco Hervé, a Chilean geologist who made an important contribution to the knowledge of the geology of Chile and the Antarctic Peninsula.

facts.statement: Unlike other tylosaurines, Kaikaifilu possesses heterodont dentition.
facts.quote: Unlike other tylosaurines, an heterodont dentition is seen in Kaikaifilu.

facts.statement: Four distinct tooth types are known: medium conical teeth without wear facets, medium conical teeth with wear facets, very large conical teeth without wear facets, and small blunt D-shaped teeth with soft enamel.
facts.quote: Four types of teeth are known from the animal: conical teeth of medium size without any wear facets, medium-sized conical teeth with two or three wear facets on their outer and inner faces, very large conical teeth without any wear facets, and small, relatively blunt D-shaped teeth with soft enamel (which may have represent developing teeth).

facts.statement: The pterygoid bone in Kaikaifilu is pointed in the rostral direction, an unusual feature among mosasaurs.
facts.quote: The pterygoid appears to be pointed in the rostral direction, which is unusual among mosasaurs.

facts.statement: Unlike its contemporary Moanasaurus, Kaikaifilu features a pre-orbital constriction of the rostrum.
facts.quote: Unlike its contemporary Moanasaurus, Kaikaifilu bears a pre-orbital constriction of the rostrum.

facts.statement: As of 2019, the classification of Kaikaifilu within the subfamily Tylosaurinae has been questioned by researchers.
facts.quote: As of 2019, just two years after its official description, the attribution of Kaikaifilu to the Tylosaurinae has been questioned.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that certain observed characteristics of Kaikaifilu contradict the definition of the Tylosaurinae group.
facts.quote: The authors note that some observed characteristics do not appear to fit, or even contradict the definition of the group.

facts.statement: Kaikaifilu was an apex predator that shared its habitat with invertebrates, fish, plesiosaurs, and other mosasaurs.
facts.quote: The animal would have been an apex predator who shared its habitat with a variety of other animals, including invertebrates, fish, plesiosaurs, and also other mosasaurs.

facts.statement: Dating to the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event, Kaikaifilu is considered one of the last known mosasaurs.
facts.quote: Dating to the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event, Kaikaifilu is one of the last known mosasaurs.

facts.statement: Kaikaifilu lived during the Upper Maastrichtian in the López de Bertodano Formation on Seymour Island, Antarctic Peninsula.
facts.quote: Kaikaifilu is known from Upper Maastrichtian deposits of the López de Bertodano Formation, located on Seymour Island, Antarctic Peninsula.

facts.statement: The waters where Kaikaifilu lived were located at about 65°S, with average deep-shelf temperatures around 6°C and surface temperatures that may have dropped below freezing.
facts.quote: Located within the polar circle at around 65°S, temperatures at medium to deep-shelf water conditions would have been around 6 C on average, while sea surface temperatures may have dropped below freezing and sea ice possibly formed at times.

facts.statement: Kaikaifilu was an extinct mosasaurine reptile that lived in Antarctica during the Late Cretaceous, just before the Cretaceous-Paleogene mass extinction.
facts.quote: Kaikaifilu es un género extinto de reptil mosasáurido tilosaurino que vivió durante el Cretácico Superior en la Antártida, justo antes de la extinción masiva del Cretácico-Terciario.

facts.statement: In 2011, the Chilean Paleontological Expedition collected a large mosasaur skull, associated jaw fragments, a partial humerus, and nearly 30 isolated teeth from the upper layers of the López de Bertodano Formation on Seymour Island, Antarctica.
facts.quote: En 2011, la Expedición Paleontológica Chilena recolectó un gran cráneo de mosasáurido, fragmentos asociados de mandíbula, un húmero parcial, y cerca de 30 dientes aislados de las capas superiores de la Formación Lopez de Bertodano en la Isla Seymour, Antártida.

facts.statement: The specimen, cataloged as SGO.PV.6509, was found in rocks dating to the late Maastrichtian, about 200 meters below the Cretaceous-Paleogene boundary.
facts.quote: El espécimen, catalogado como SGO.PV.6509, fue hallado en rocas que datan de finales de la época del Maastrichtiense, cerca de 200 metros debajo del límite entre el Cretácico y el Paleógeno.

facts.statement: The species was named Kaikaifilu hervei in honor of "Kai-Kai filú", a reptilian ocean deity from Mapuche cosmology, and Dr. Francisco Hervé, a Chilean geologist.
facts.quote: El espécimen fue denominado como Kaikaifilu hervei en honor de "Kai-Kai filú", una deidad oceánica reptiliana de la cosmología del pueblo mapuche y el dr. Francisco Hervé, un geólogo chileno quien ha contribuido significativamente al estudio de la geología chilena y antártica.

facts.statement: The preserved skull parts of the Kaikaifilu holotype measure about 0.7 meters long, suggesting a total skull length of 1.1 to 1.2 meters.
facts.quote: Las partes preservadas del cráneo en el holotipo de Kaikaifilu miden unos 0.7 metros de largo, lo que sugiere una longitud craneana total de entre 1.1 a 1.2 metros.

facts.statement: This skull size exceeds that of contemporary mosasaurs, including Taniwhasaurus antarcticus, which had a skull length of 65 centimeters.
facts.quote: Esto excede la talla de otros mosasáuridos contemporáneos, incluyendo a Taniwhasaurus antarcticus, el cual tenía una longitud craneana de 65 centímetros.

facts.statement: Kaikaifilu has a prominent crest on the upper margin of the eye orbit and another crest between the two nostrils, unlike Taniwhasaurus.
facts.quote: Tiene una cresta prominente en el margen superior de la órbita ocular, y además posee otra cresta entre las dos narinas (a diferencia de Taniwhasaurus).

facts.statement: Kaikaifilu had heterodont dentition, featuring medium conical teeth without wear facets, medium conical teeth with two or three wear facets, very large conical teeth without wear facets, and small blunt teeth with D-shaped cross-sections and soft enamel likely representing growing teeth.
facts.quote: Es notorio además que los dientes de Kaikaifilu sean heterodontos, lo que significa que tenía más de un tipo diferente de diente en su boca: dientes cónicos de tamaño mediano sin ninguna faceta de desgaste; dientes cónicos de tamaño medio con dos o tres facetas de desgaste en sus superficies interna y externa; dientes cónicos muy grandes sin ninguna faceta de desgaste; y dientes pequeños relativamente romos con secciones transversales en forma de letra D y con esmalte suave (los cuales probablemente se traten de dientes en crecimiento).

facts.statement: Only one other mosasaur, Eremiasaurus from Morocco, is known to have heterodont dentition.
facts.quote: Solo se conoce a otro mosasáurido con dentadura heterodonta, Eremiasaurus de Marruecos.

facts.statement: The genus Kaikaifilu was described by Otero et al. in 2016.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Otero et al., 2016

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Kaikaifilu is Kaikaifilu hervei.
facts.quote: type_species: Kaikaifilu hervei

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses show that Kaikaifilu is closely related to Tylosaurus and Taniwhasaurus within the subfamily Tylosaurinae.
facts.quote: Todos ellos muestran que estaba cercanamente relacionado con Tylosaurus y Taniwhasaurus en la subfamilia Tylosaurinae.

facts.statement: Kaikaifilu belongs to the parent group Tylosaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Tylosaurinae

facts.statement: Kaikaifilu is classified in the family Mosasauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Mosasauridae

facts.statement: Due to its large size, Kaikaifilu was likely an apex predator that preyed on plesiosaurs from the formation.
facts.quote: Plesiosaurs from this formation would have been potential prey for Kaikaifilu, which, due to its large size, would probably have been an apex predator.

facts.statement: Fish fossils in the López de Bertodano Formation are dominated by Enchodus and ichthyodectiformes.
facts.quote: The fish fossils located in the López de Bertodano Formation are dominated by Enchodus and ichthyodectiformes.

facts.statement: Kaikaifilu lived alongside the aristonectine plesiosaur Aristonectes.
facts.quote: Kaikaifilu además vivió junto al plesiosaurio aristonectino Aristonectes.
